summary: Read the owning person's availability and directive note from MCP and ChatGPT: fractal_availability_get over a new read.assistant.availability scope

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery changes.

schema.detail: No stored schema, index, or data changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint or digest rule changes.

compatibility.detail: Adds the optional assistant scope read.assistant.availability and the assistant read projection GET /v1/client/assistant/availability, admitted only for grants that hold the scope and authorized per read like every other assistant projection. It accepts only max_response_bytes and returns kind person-availability with the grant issuer's own PersonAvailability without raw device presence (presence and presence_observed_at are null; an assistant is not the person; status_source is override, presence or unreported), current DirectiveNote or null, and directive_note_truncated; no parameter selects another person. The availability fields are never cut; the note text is cut on a character boundary to fit max_response_bytes with its whole envelope, and directive_note_truncated is then true, so a default 4096-byte read of a long note still succeeds instead of failing response-budget-exceeded; read again with max_response_bytes up to 16384 for the whole note. The MCP and ChatGPT adapters list fractal_availability_get after fractal_agents_list, with directive_note_truncated required in its output schema.

downtime.detail: No added startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: Existing paired assistant grants do not gain the scope. The configured owning person re-grants on the grant-issuer member with every scope the grant should keep plus read.assistant.availability, e.g. fractal devices --as person/operator grant policy GRANT --scope read.assistant.summary --scope read.assistant.attention --scope read.assistant.missions --scope read.assistant.agents --scope read.assistant.availability --expires-in 30d --disclose-to-openai --consent-evidence EVIDENCE. Then restart or refresh the MCP client so tools/list shows the tool.

recovery.detail: A read-only projection; removing the scope from a grant or revoking the grant ends access, and no state needs recovery.
